title: Data modelling
summary: Decide when to embed data, when to reference it, and when copying data is the right choice.

quiz.q: An order always has between 1 and 10 line items, and you always show them with the order. What is the best design?
options: Embed the items as an array inside the order
Put each item in a separate collection and join them every time
Store the items as one long string
quiz.explain: Small lists that belong to a single parent and are read together are the classic case for embedding.

quiz.q: A popular post may collect millions of comments. Which design is safer?
options: Embed all comments in the post document
Keep comments in their own collection and store postId on each comment
Store the comments in a text file
Embed only the newest comment and delete the rest
quiz.explain: An embedded array that can grow without limit will eventually hit the 16 MB document size limit and make every read of the post heavy.

quiz.q: Complete the term: storing only an id that points to a document in another collection is called a ___.
quiz.explain: A reference holds the id of another document, and `$lookup` can join it when needed.

quiz.q: Why should an order store the **price at the time of purchase** instead of only a productId?
options: Because the product's price may change later, and the order must keep what the customer paid
Because ids take more space than prices
Because referencing is not allowed in MongoDB
quiz.explain: Here a copy is a deliberate snapshot. Duplicating is good when the value should not change with its source.

quiz.q: A customer's phone number is copied into 5,000 old orders. What is the main downside?
options: When the number changes, all 5,000 copies must be updated or they will be out of date
quiz.explain: Duplicated data has to be kept in sync by your code. That is the price you pay for faster reads.

exercise.task:
Model an order by inserting **one** document into the `orders` collection using `insertOne`. The document must have:

- `orderNo`: `'A100'`
- `customer`: an embedded object `{ name: 'Asha', city: 'Madurai' }`
- `items`: an embedded array of two objects, each with `sku`, `qty` and `price`:
  - `PEN`, quantity 2, price 10
  - `BOOK`, quantity 1, price 50
hints: Call `db.orders.insertOne({ ... })` with one object that has three fields.
`customer` is an object in curly braces. `items` is an array in square brackets that holds two objects.
